internal.courseworkclassoption: Class option forwarding and filtering helper.

entries.name: courseworksetup
entries.description: Sets course metadata and output configuration, updating the supplied values while leaving the others unchanged. Fonts load with the class, so select them through a class option.
entries.arguments: Supply comma-separated keys, with braces around values that contain commas or LaTeX. See the setup key table for available keys and defaults.

entries.name: courseworkvalue
entries.description: Expands one of the six metadata values. It reads metadata only, not modes, page-break settings, or fonts.
entries.arguments: `key` is one of `author`, `course-code`, `course-title`, `term`, `textbook`, or `textbook-author`. All six values default to empty.

entries.name: makecourseworktitle
entries.description: Produces a title with the course title, code, author, and date. Contents and assignment headings are added separately.
entries.arguments: `title` is optional and defaults to empty; `date` defaults to the configured term. Set page breaks and page numbers explicitly in the front matter.

entries.name: makeassignmentheading
entries.description: Produces an assignment heading with the author and title on the left, and the course title and date on the right. The current page uses an empty page style.
entries.arguments: `title` is optional and defaults to empty; `date` defaults to the configured term. Set page breaks and page numbers explicitly in the front matter.

entries.name: assignment
entries.description: Starts a new assignment and resets its declarations. Each assignment must have an ID unique within the document.
entries.arguments:
`title` is the assignment heading. The required `id` must start with a letter or digit, followed by letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores.

The required `directory` is a path relative to the project root. `number` must be a positive integer and defaults to the next assignment number. `problems-title` defaults to `Problem Set`.

entries.name: declareproblem
entries.description: Declares a problem with a stable ID and an optional display title without reading its fragments. Declare it after the assignment and before printing the assignment.
entries.arguments: `id` follows the assignment ID character rules and must be unique within the assignment. `title` defaults to empty.

entries.name: printassignment
entries.description: Prints the current assignment. For every role, selected problems are numbered from 1 in the specified order. Canonical labels use `prob:<assignment-id>:<problem-id>`, and reference values include the assignment number.
entries.arguments: `problems` is a comma-separated list of IDs. An omitted or empty value selects all problems in declaration order. Duplicate or unknown IDs, an assignment without problems, missing required files, or attempts to print an assignment more than once cause errors.

entries.name: priming
entries.description: Typesets a short priming paragraph with a bold italic label.
entries.arguments: `text` supplies the content after the label.

entries.name: procedure
entries.description: Typesets a short procedure paragraph with a bold italic label.
entries.arguments: `text` supplies the content after the label.

entries.name: NN
entries.description: Typesets the symbol for natural numbers in blackboard bold, in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: ZZ
entries.description: Typesets the symbol for integers in blackboard bold, in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: QQ
entries.description: Typesets the symbol for rational numbers in blackboard bold, in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: RR
entries.description: Typesets the symbol for real numbers in blackboard bold, in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: CC
entries.description: Typesets the symbol for complex numbers in blackboard bold, in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: dd
entries.description: Typesets an upright differential d in math mode.
entries.arguments: No arguments. Write the variable separately and add any required spacing.

entries.name: deriv
entries.description: Typesets an ordinary derivative using `diffcoeff` in math mode.
entries.arguments: `order` defaults to 1, and `variable` is the differentiation variable. Leave `expression` empty to form an operator. A following bracketed expression is not consumed as an evaluation point.

entries.name: pderiv
entries.description: Typesets a partial derivative using `diffcoeff` in math mode.
entries.arguments: `order` defaults to 1, and `variable` is the differentiation variable. Leave `expression` empty to form an operator. A following bracketed expression is not consumed as an evaluation point.

entries.name: integral
entries.description: Typesets an integral with an upright differential in text or math mode. The size option changes only the integral sign: `medium` and `large` enlarge the display sign by one and two `relsize` steps, respectively. Nested calls default to `normal`.
entries.arguments: `size` defaults to `normal`; unknown sizes cause errors. All four braced arguments are required, but empty `lower` or `upper` arguments omit the corresponding bounds.

entries.name: evalat
entries.description: Typesets an expression evaluated at two bounds, using a right evaluation bar in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` is the expression to evaluate, and `lower` and `upper` are the endpoints. Either endpoint can be empty.

entries.name: evalbracket
entries.description: Typesets an expression evaluated at two bounds, using a left square bracket and a right evaluation bar in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` is the expression to evaluate, and `lower` and `upper` are the endpoints. Either endpoint can be empty.

entries.name: paren
entries.description: Typesets paired parentheses in math mode. The unstarred form uses a fixed size, while the starred form sizes the delimiters automatically.
entries.arguments: `expression` is the enclosed content. For an explicit size, use an optional argument such as `\big` or `\Big` instead of the star.

entries.name: bracket
entries.description: Typesets paired square brackets in math mode. The unstarred form uses a fixed size, while the starred form sizes the delimiters automatically.
entries.arguments: `expression` is the enclosed content. For an explicit size, use an optional argument such as `\big` or `\Big` instead of the star.

entries.name: abs
entries.description: Typesets paired absolute-value bars in math mode. The unstarred form uses a fixed size, while the starred form sizes the delimiters automatically.
entries.arguments: `expression` is the enclosed content. For an explicit size, use an optional argument such as `\big` or `\Big` instead of the star.

entries.name: norm
entries.description: Typesets paired norm bars in math mode. The unstarred form uses a fixed size, while the starred form sizes the delimiters automatically.
entries.arguments: `expression` is the enclosed content. For an explicit size, use an optional argument such as `\big` or `\Big` instead of the star.

entries.name: average
entries.description: Typesets an average in angle brackets in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` is the enclosed content. For covariance, put a pair such as `X,Y` in the same argument.

entries.name: expectation
entries.description: Typesets expectation E with square brackets in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` is the enclosed content. For covariance, put a pair such as `X,Y` in the same argument.

entries.name: variance
entries.description: Typesets variance Var with fixed-size parentheses in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` is the enclosed content. For covariance, put a pair such as `X,Y` in the same argument.

entries.name: covariance
entries.description: Typesets covariance Cov with automatically sized parentheses in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` is the enclosed content. For covariance, put a pair such as `X,Y` in the same argument.

entries.name: probability
entries.description: Typesets probability P with automatically sized parentheses in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` is the enclosed content. For covariance, put a pair such as `X,Y` in the same argument.

entries.name: conditionalprob
entries.description: Typesets a conditional probability with an automatically sized middle bar in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: `event` and `condition` are the event and condition expressions.

entries.name: mathbold
entries.description: Typesets bold mathematics in text or math mode using `bm` for legacy mathematics or the Unicode bold alphabet with `unicode-math`. Nested upright and italic alphabets retain their shape.
entries.arguments: `expression` can be a symbol or a complete mathematics expression.

entries.name: slashfrac
entries.description: Typesets a compact slash fraction with a raised numerator and lowered denominator in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: `numerator` and `denominator` supply mathematics expressions.

entries.name: mathtext
entries.description: Inserts text between half-em spaces in math mode.
entries.arguments: `text` is typeset with `\text`. The optional `prefix` defaults to empty and can contain punctuation such as a comma.

entries.name: combinations
entries.description: Typesets n choose k in C notation in math mode.
entries.arguments: `n` is the total count, and `k` is the selected count.

entries.name: permutations
entries.description: Typesets n-permute-k in P notation in math mode.
entries.arguments: `n` is the total count, and `k` is the selected count.

entries.name: colvector
entries.description: Typesets a column array in parentheses in math mode.
entries.arguments: `alignment` defaults to `r`; `l` and `c` are also available. Separate rows with `\\`.

entries.name: questioneq
entries.description: Typesets an equals sign with a question mark above it in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: checkeq
entries.description: Typesets an equals sign with a check mark above it in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: crosseq
entries.description: Typesets an equals sign with a cross above it in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: vect
entries.description: Typesets a bold vector using the active mathematics backend in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: `symbol` is the vector symbol; Greek letters work if the font supports them.

entries.name: uprightvect
entries.description: Typesets an upright bold vector using the active mathematics backend in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: `symbol` is the vector symbol; Greek letters work if the font supports them.

entries.name: unitvect
entries.description: Typesets a bold vector with a hat using the active mathematics backend in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: `symbol` is the vector symbol; Greek letters work if the font supports them.

entries.name: uprightunitvect
entries.description: Typesets an upright bold vector with a hat using the active mathematics backend in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: `symbol` is the vector symbol; Greek letters work if the font supports them.

entries.name: xhat
entries.description: Typesets an upright x unit vector with a bold hat in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: yhat
entries.description: Typesets an upright y unit vector with a bold hat in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: zhat
entries.description: Typesets an upright z unit vector with a bold hat in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: rhat
entries.description: Typesets an upright r unit vector with a bold hat in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: shat
entries.description: Typesets an upright s unit vector with a bold hat in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: thetahat
entries.description: Typesets a theta unit vector with a bold hat in math mode, using the active Greek mathematics alphabet.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: phihat
entries.description: Typesets a phi unit vector with a bold hat in math mode, using the active Greek mathematics alphabet.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: grad
entries.description: Typesets a bold nabla gradient operator in math mode without consuming the following expression.
entries.arguments: No arguments. Write the function or field after the command.

entries.name: laplacian
entries.description: Typesets a bold squared nabla followed by a thin space in math mode.
entries.arguments: No arguments. Write the function or field after the command.

entries.name: separation
entries.description: Typesets script r for separation notation in text or math mode, using the bundled PDF glyphs.
entries.arguments: No arguments. Both glyph PDFs must be available through kpathsea.

entries.name: separationvect
entries.description: Typesets bold script r for separation notation in text or math mode, using the bundled PDF glyphs.
entries.arguments: No arguments. Both glyph PDFs must be available through kpathsea.

entries.name: separationunit
entries.description: Typesets bold script r with a hat for separation notation in text or math mode, using the bundled PDF glyphs.
entries.arguments: No arguments. Both glyph PDFs must be available through kpathsea.

entries.name: volumeregion
entries.description: Typesets the volume domain symbol v in math mode, using `txmi` glyphs with the legacy backend or ordinary italic letters with the Unicode backend.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: surfaceregion
entries.description: Typesets the surface domain symbol s in math mode, using `txmi` glyphs with the legacy backend or ordinary italic letters with the Unicode backend.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: pathregion
entries.description: Typesets the path domain symbol p in math mode, using `txmi` glyphs with the legacy backend or ordinary italic letters with the Unicode backend.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: kB
entries.description: Typesets the Boltzmann constant symbol without a numeric value, in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: NA
entries.description: Typesets the Avogadro constant symbol without a numeric value, in text or math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: dbar
entries.description: Typesets a barred differential symbol for an inexact differential in math mode.
entries.arguments: No arguments. Write the quantity after the command.

entries.name: constantvalue
entries.description: Typesets a rounded constant with SI units in text or math mode: 1.381 × 10⁻²³ J/K or 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹. These are the existing library values rather than exact SI definitions.
entries.arguments: The required `name` is `boltzmann` or `avogadro`; other names cause errors.

entries.name: theorem
entries.description: Shares the theorem counter, which resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Use a standard `\label` in the body for references.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: lemma
entries.description: Shares the theorem counter, which resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Use a standard `\label` in the body for references.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.description: Shares the theorem counter, which resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Use a standard `\label` in the body for references.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.description: Shares the theorem counter, which resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Use a standard `\label` in the body for references.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: conjecture
entries.description: Shares the theorem counter, which resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Use a standard `\label` in the body for references.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: algorithm
entries.description: Shares the theorem counter, which resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Use a standard `\label` in the body for references.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: definition
entries.description: Uses its own counter, which resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Use a standard `\label` in the body for references.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: example
entries.description: Uses its own counter, which resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Use a standard `\label` in the body for references.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: remark
entries.description: Uses its own counter, which resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Use a standard `\label` in the body for references.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: summary
entries.description: Uses its own counter, which resets by subsection. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Use a standard `\label` in the body for references.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: note
entries.description: Produces an unnumbered block. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: caveat
entries.description: Produces an unnumbered block. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: warning
entries.description: Produces an unnumbered block. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: question
entries.description: Produces an unnumbered block. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: speculation
entries.description: Produces an unnumbered block. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument.
entries.arguments: Accepts an optional title and a body containing ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: proof
entries.description: Typesets an unnumbered proof with a closing marker, using the `amsthm` environment loaded by `courseenvironments`.
entries.arguments: The optional title replaces `Proof`. If the proof ends with a display, use `\qedhere` inside the display as needed.

entries.name: formula
entries.description: Typesets a mathematics display with a bold text tag and a separate sequential formula counter. References return the counter value independently of the displayed tag. The counter runs across sections, and the environment does not force a following line break.
entries.arguments: The optional tag defaults to `Formula N`. The body is already in math mode; put `\label` inside the environment.

entries.name: subparts
entries.description: Typesets a list of subparts labelled (a), (b), and so on.
entries.arguments: No arguments. Start each part with `\item`.

entries.name: mathtable
entries.description: Typesets a floating table containing a mathematics array with an automatic top rule. Options affect only the current table.
entries.arguments:
`columns` is the array alignment. `caption` and `label` default to empty, and a label requires a caption. `placement` defaults to `ht!`, or `H` in notes.

Supply row endings and add `\bottomrule` if needed.

entries.name: tableheading
entries.description: Typesets a centered, two-line text heading for a mathematics table column.
entries.arguments: `top` and `bottom` contain text; put dollar signs around any mathematics.

entries.name: courseenvironmentsetup
entries.description: Sets global defaults for subsequent mathematics tables. Notes default to placement `H` and top skip `-2ex`; other contexts default to `ht!` and `-1em`.
entries.arguments: `table-placement` is the LaTeX float placement, and `table-top-skip` is a TeX length or skip.
